title: Surjectivity of the restriction algebra map
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $P=\pi_0(\operatorname{Spec}A)$ be the quotient space whose points are the maximal connected subsets of $\operatorname{Spec}A$, and let $\pi:\operatorname{Spec}A\to P$ be the quotient map [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $T\subseteq P$ be any subset. For each clopen (open and closed) subset $W\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$ containing $\pi^{-1}(T)$, let $e_W$ be the unique idempotent ($e_W^2=e_W$) with $D(e_W)=W$, [lem-weil-pbc-spec-clopen-idempotent], where $D(e)=\{\mathfrak p:e\notin\mathfrak p\}$. Define $B=\operatorname{Restriction}_A(T)=\varinjlim_W A_{e_W}$ in the category of commutative $A$-algebras [def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], indexed by these clopens in reverse inclusion with their canonical localization transition maps, and write $v:A\to B$ for the canonical map. Then $v$ is surjective.
